page: Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is an entry-level compute instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a single dedicated physical core from an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU configuration lacks simultaneous multithreading, providing 1 vCPU backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory and storage configurations are generous relative to the core count, providing 8.0 GB of system RAM—a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of memory-optimized profiles. The server bundles 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reflects pronounced single-thread capability counterbalanced by core count limitations. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 3,373.08, placing in the top 10 percent of recorded results, and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,956. Single-threaded compression throughput is similarly competitive, reaching 31.57 GB/sec in gzip. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth register in the mid-range at 40.43 GB/sec and 36.8 GB/sec respectively. However, total multi-core capacity ranks low due to the single-core topology, producing 1,930 in multi-core Geekbench and lower overall throughput in parallel tasks such as Clang compilation and static web serving.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides dedicated AMD EPYC execution and substantial local NVMe storage without resource sharing or CPU credit throttling. It serves as an effective platform for low-concurrency workloads that demand high per-thread performance and substantial memory, such as standalone Redis instances, small relational databases, background batch processors, and single-worker data ingestion pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-s-1c-8gb-150s-amd is a single-core instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute series, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. Built with a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the system pairs its single vCPU with 8.0 GB of RAM and 150 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, along with one public IPv4 address and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics reaching the top 10 percent and strong single-thread gzip compression throughput of 31.57 GB/sec. However, total parallel compute capacity remains constrained by the single physical core architecture, resulting in low multi-core benchmark rankings. With dedicated compute allocation and high memory per core, this instance is suitable for lightweight database services, single-threaded backend tasks, caching nodes, and memory-dependent development or staging environments.
